nodes.label: x-editor Implementation Plan
Product thesis: guidance is the product, not a layer over a validator
nodes.rationale: No validator exposes the content-model state machine needed to answer position-sensitive questions mid-edit. A team that treats guidance as a thin layer over a validator discovers in month five that it cannot be built that way and ships an expert tool by accident.

nodes.label: Schema-aware guidance engine (packages/xsd)
Stated non-goals: phones, collaboration, text editor, server
nodes.rationale: Stated explicitly so they are decisions rather than omissions.

nodes.label: Verification status audit trail
nodes.rationale: Research agents had no network access, so their package claims were model recall; everything load-bearing was re-verified against primary sources and anything unverified is a spike rather than a decision.

nodes.label: Stack: boring choices, novelty budget spent on the schema engine
nodes.rationale: React 19 for ecosystem depth in virtualized tree/overlays/command palette; Vite for module-worker and WASM handling; CodeMirror 6 over Monaco at ~10x smaller; rejected Next.js, Redux Toolkit, MUI/Mantine, react-arborist.

nodes.label: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM
nodes.rationale: The browser DOM destroys data silently — expands entity references, drops the DOCTYPE internal subset, never emits the XML declaration, rewrites to , normalises attribute quoting, invents namespace prefixes. Users keep these files in git and a reformat-on-save produces a 4,000-line diff and gets the tool banned.

nodes.label: Splice serializer: slice clean subtrees verbatim
nodes.rationale: Makes byte-exact round-tripping structural rather than a matter of getting a hundred formatting details right, and makes serialisation O(changed) rather than O(document).

nodes.label: Labelled command log with inverses
nodes.rationale: Human-readable labels generated at construction time are what make a visible History panel possible; quick fixes return commands too, so a fix is atomically undoable as one step. Undo always moves focus and scrolls to the affected node — silent undo is the top complaint about prior art.

nodes.label: State split: command log, Zustand, XState
nodes.rationale: XState used narrowly for exactly three flows where boolean-flag soup would otherwise emerge — the wizard, drag-and-drop, and the validation lifecycle. Stable NodeIds mean selection, expansion and validation results survive edits.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled typed worker protocol
nodes.rationale: Rather than Comlink: revision tagging and terminate-and-respawn cancellation are exactly what Comlink's transparent-proxy model hides. Stale results render dimmed rather than cleared so the UI never flickers to 'no problems' mid-edit.

nodes.label: XSD 1.1 in scope, our engine is the primary verdict
nodes.rationale: No JavaScript XSD 1.1 validator exists; libxml2 is 1.0-only and its maintainer says 1.1 is not planned. The saving grace is that the schema engine was always being written anyway, and the two headline 1.1 features are XPath-shaped so fontoxpath (already mandatory for Schematron) makes assertions cheap.

nodes.label: libxml2-wasm as the fast XSD 1.0 differential oracle
xmlschema under Pyodide as the authoritative XSD 1.1 oracle
nodes.rationale: Pure Python with only elementpath as a dependency, so micropip installs it under Pyodide with no C extensions to cross-compile. Heavy (~6-10MB) so it loads lazily in its own worker behind an explicit user action; in CI it runs under plain CPython and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Differential harness dispatches on the schema's declared version
nodes.rationale: A 1.1-legal schema can be UPA-invalid under 1.0, so a 1.0 oracle pointed at a 1.1 schema drowns the harness in false failures. Version dispatch does not trust vc:minVersion — a schema using 1.1 constructs is 1.1 whether or not it says so.

nodes.label: Direct Schematron interpreter over fontoxpath, not XSLT
nodes.rationale: Better on four axes: no XSLT engine to break in November 2026; fontoxpath is a mandatory dependency regardless so the marginal cost is one module; findings bind to nodes by identity rather than an SVRL @location string; per-rule statistics become possible. Written from scratch rather than forked from node-schematron because the reusable parts are the ones our CST and XPath facade already provide.

nodes.label: Chrome removes XSLT in v158 (17 Nov 2026)
nodes.rationale: Any design depending on the browser's XSLTProcessor has a hard expiry date; Firefox and WebKit have signalled they will follow. The alternative runtime SaxonJS 2 is free of charge but proprietary, an easy trap since 'free' reads as 'open source'.

nodes.label: Error to node mapping: own the serializer, return a lineMap
nodes.rationale: Emit exactly one element start-tag per line when serialising for validation so libxml2's 'line 42' is an O(1) array lookup, and column numbers — which libxml2 reports as 0 for schema errors — become irrelevant.

nodes.label: Risk 1: guidance/verdict drift
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine and libxml2 are two independent implementations of XSD semantics; disagreement means the product actively teaches beginners wrong things, which destroys the value proposition. Mitigated structurally by differential CI from Phase 3 day one and a published pass rate.

nodes.label: Risk 4: bundle weight and the entry-chunk regression
nodes.rationale: A stray top-level import pulling a validator into the main chunk is a one-line mistake that costs every user the download and looks like nothing. It has already happened once — XSD 1.1 assertions statically imported fontoxpath and put 330KB into the entry chunk — so it is checked mechanically rather than remembered.

nodes.label: Risk 6: memory, not CPU, is the ceiling
nodes.rationale: A 50MB instance expands to 400-600MB inside the wasm32 heap and browsers OOM well below the 4GB limit; mitigation is a stated threshold policy with graceful degradation, not 'we'll optimise later'.

nodes.label: Risk 7: File System Access API is Chromium-only
nodes.rationale: ~28% of users get save-in-place and Firefox calls it 'harmful', so the download/upload path is designed as primary with FSA as progressive enhancement, not the reverse. OPFS for autosave works everywhere.

nodes.label: Three-file workspace: one slot per kind (xml, xsd, sch)
nodes.rationale: An earlier design had attach-a-schema, edit-a-schema and attach-a-sample as three separate mechanisms and could not express cross-file errors; it also had a silent hole where Schematron rules were parsed from whichever document was being edited, so the bundled failing-rule example opened green. A test calling runSchematron directly could not see it.

nodes.label: A file is filed by its root element, not its extension
nodes.rationale: The extension is a claim; the root element is a fact, and somebody handed rules.xml should not have to rename it before the editor will run it.

nodes.label: Findings are attributed to the file they belong in
nodes.rationale: A failing assert belongs to the XML; a rule whose XPath does not evaluate belongs to the .sch; a dangling type= belongs to the XSD even though it is noticed in the XML. Filing a rule error against the XML would send someone editing a document they have not broken.

nodes.label: Downstream re-derivation tiered by cost
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine recompiles in-process and synchronously so schema edits show up immediately; libxml2's schema is debounced at 500ms because setSchema terminates and respawns the worker; Schematron rules are guarded on their serialized source so typing in the XML does not reparse the .sch.

nodes.label: The Insert palette
nodes.rationale: The most important screen in the product; insertion is rendered three ways at once (ghost row, toolbar button, four key bindings) so it cannot be missed.

nodes.label: The Inspector is the selection inspector
nodes.rationale: Everything about the selected node in one fixed place is the property beginners rely on most; sections come from a per-document-kind registry so XSD and Schematron swap sections in without a second layout. Read-only projections go on the left, deliberately away from the controls that change the document.

nodes.label: The teaching promise cannot depend on authored documentation
nodes.rationale: Most schemas a beginner meets have no annotations at all, so describe.ts always returns a sentence generated from the compiled model. Generated descriptions are marked auto so users learn to distinguish authored guidance from inferred.

nodes.label: Expert mode removes chrome, never capability
nodes.rationale: Ship the toggle on day one and make every UI decision answer 'which side of the toggle?', or beginner scaffolding accretes until the tool is slow for everyone.

nodes.label: One model, three projections — never a second editable model
nodes.rationale: The XSD component tree and the Schematron semantic tree are derived projections over the same CST; every sync bug in this class of tool lives in the gap between two representations of one document.

nodes.label: A schema is a graph written as a tree
nodes.rationale: type="Address" is a reference the outline cannot draw, which is why every XSD refactoring exists — each one means 'find all the edges yourself and get none of them wrong'.

nodes.label: Refactorings find references syntactically, not from the compiled model
nodes.rationale: Renaming has to work on a schema that does not currently compile, which is the state a schema is in for most of the time anyone is editing it. References come from a table of the twelve QName-valued attributes kept in their six symbol spaces, because ref means three different things depending on the element it sits on.

nodes.label: Three things the refactorings refuse to do
nodes.rationale: Inline a shared type, extract under a taken name, and extract when no correct reference text exists — because the alternative in each case is a confident wrong answer. A round-trip test asserts extract-then-inline returns the file byte-for-byte.

nodes.label: A generated document is valid and meaningless
nodes.rationale: The failure mode of every document generator, invisible without help: the badge reads green while every date says 2026-01-01. So the scaffolder marks every invented value, F7 steps through them, and fixed/default values are not marked because the schema author already decided those.

nodes.label: Placeholder review state is derived, not tracked
nodes.rationale: Comparing against the document is exact, costs one pass, and gets undo right for free; an intercept-the-edit scheme silently loses entries, and a test pins that case.

nodes.label: Smart paste asks before the edit
nodes.rationale: Each option's cost is measured and ranked by consequence then proximity; plain Ctrl+V goes straight through when exactly one option is valid, because turning an expert's paste into a dialogue is its own failure. The fragment is reconstructed node by node rather than regenerated from the schema, after an earlier version produced correct elements containing none of the clipboard.

nodes.label: Schema inference: permissive where evidence is thin
nodes.rationale: Anything seen twice is written unbounded because permitting one more than the file showed is a smaller mistake than rejecting the next file; every value stays xs:string because guessing xs:date from one date-shaped string rejects documents the author would have accepted. Framed as a draft with per-decision evidence, never as authoritative.

nodes.label: Three bundled examples, one lesson each
nodes.rationale: Purchase order teaches the core loop; the topic teaches prefixes and mixed content across two namespaces and an import; the invoice is structurally perfect and wrong (total 120.00 against lines summing to 140.00). A test asserts it fails exactly one rule and goes green when corrected, so CI catches a broken first-minute demo rather than a user.

nodes.label: A mixed element is one tree row carrying its flow
nodes.rationale: SPIKE-4 asked the wrong question: both candidates were editors and the unusable part was the display. Marked-up runs show as angle-bracket ellipses rather than being stripped, so it is never a surprise that half a sentence is tagged, and the children stay reachable. ProseMirror was declined for ~150KB in the entry chunk plus a second document model.

nodes.label: FlowEditor seam (flowSource / setFlow)
nodes.rationale: The whole interface between the flow and the document, so a WYSIWYG surface can replace it later without anything else moving.

nodes.label: Table view for repeated siblings
nodes.rationale: Reading down a column is the question a tree makes hard and a grid makes free. Columns accumulate across rows so one row missing an optional child does not lose the column, and an absent cell's element is created on first edit. Nested children never become columns because their meaning would differ by depth.

nodes.label: Hand-written offline service worker
nodes.rationale: Part of the security story rather than a nicety — the premise is that documents never leave the browser, and a validator that stops working on a train contradicts its own claim. Hand-written rather than vite-plugin-pwa because the requirement is 'cache these seven files' and a dependency whose configuration surface exceeds the thing it configures is a liability. The cache name carries a content hash so a new build invalidates the old cache wholesale.

nodes.label: First-run coach marks, never modal
nodes.rationale: Everything underneath stays clickable so someone who would rather just start is never blocked by the explanation of how to start; Escape dismisses all of them, because a person pressing Escape is telling you they do not want the tour.

nodes.label: i18n deliberately deferred
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string is written to be read, and threading them through a message catalogue is a refactor that should happen when there is a second locale to test against, not before.

nodes.label: xs:openContent never reaches the automaton
nodes.rationale: Interleaving the whole model with a wildcard loop is a state explosion, when the same semantics fall out of removing the wildcard-matched children before the model runs.

nodes.label: Security model: client-side is not a security property
Open decisions: DTD/RELAX NG support, document size
nodes.rationale: 50MB+ files change the architecture (streaming, partial loading) rather than just the tuning; opening a DTD- or RELAX NG-based document should at minimum give a clear 'not supported'.

hyperedges.label: One CST, projections never a second model
